The folder next/packages/libfabrika/src/node/repositories joins the vi lock (0555, 0579) as option (b): two new override blocks in .oxlintrc.json, written after the JSON.parse warn blocks, not added to the oxlint-plugins/** block. So block one covers the whole folder (vitest rule, six entries, five vi entries) and block two, for its files but *.test.ts, writes the eight entries plus the five vi ones. Both are at error and not warn as the plan's sketch says: a warn line with no fire left in its folder fails pnpm lint (advice.ts, stale), and the folder has no JSON.parse fire. So JSON.parse is blocking there now; it was advice only. V1 is one new scenario in oxlint-plugins/plants.test.ts that reads --print-config, takes every glob of every block that sets vitest/no-restricted-vi-methods, plants a product, a test-support and a test path in each, and holds the vi lines (the union of VI_METHODS and VI_PROPERTIES) and each entry the folder took before (REFLECT, TAGGED_ERROR, a JSON.parse line, PROCESS_OUTPUT in libfabrika's files but its tests), including the JSON.parse severity. V2: the plain alias v.spyOn(console, "log") after import { vi as v } is refused by the vitest rule (a planted line of V1, in VI_LOCK). The alias with a chained call, v.spyOn(console, "warn").mockImplementation(...), is refused by neither half of the pair: it is planted as a line that passes with a comment, and the gap is a finding row (in the report; the lead saves it). L10 of the Reflect ban in plants.test.ts lists the blocks that hold the ban for next/ in order, so it now lists the two new blocks before client/. README row for the lock updated. No commit and no push in this run: another pull request owns .oxlintrc.json, so the changes stay uncommitted for the lead.
